title: Console: A/B testing results dashboard (variant comparison, confidence indicators, filters, a11y)
creator: Tessa Morgan
description:
Design the Console results experience for route-level A/B experiments.

The Results dashboard must help customers answer: “Is Variant B better or worse than A (control) for my production route?” across the core standardized metrics (latency, TTFT, cost, errors) and optional quality metrics (offline eval suite deltas).

Scope (v1 / beta):
- Summary header: experiment name/id, route, status (draft/running/paused/stopped), started/ended timestamps, traffic split, eligibility (project/region), and ‘control’ variant.
- Variant comparison modules:
  - Latency: p50/p95/p99 and TTFT (time to first token), plus delta vs control.
  - Cost: tokens/request and estimated $/1k requests (or $/1M tokens) using Redwood metering; display delta vs control.
  - Reliability: error rate (5xx), timeout rate, 429 rate; display delta vs control.
  - Exposure volume: total exposures, exposures per variant, exposures over time.
- Confidence/interpretation UI:
  - Provide a lightweight “confidence” indicator for deltas (don’t overpromise statistical significance).
  - Clear copy when sample sizes are small, when confidence is low, or when the observation window is too short.
  - Explicitly separate “observed change” from “causal claim”; add tooltip that results are observational with guardrails.
- Filtering and breakdowns:
  - Time range picker (last 1h / 24h / 7d / custom), with timezone handling.
  - Filters: region, model, deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated), and route (when viewing from project-level entry point).
  - Optional breakdown toggles: by region (small multiples) and by response type (streaming vs non-streaming) if present in schema.
- A11y requirements:
  - All charts must have table equivalents or accessible summaries (screen reader-friendly).
  - Color contrast: do not rely on red/green for deltas; use iconography + text + patterns.
  - Keyboard navigation for filters, tabs, tooltips, and chart focus states.
  - Support reduced motion; avoid auto-animating line charts.

Non-goals (v1):
- Custom metric ingestion and fully user-defined dashboards.
- Multi-armed bandit recommendations.
- Deep “per-request trace” browsing (link out to existing tracing views instead).

Artifacts / references:
- PRD + GA criteria: sources/linear/product-management/PM-481-route-level-ab-testing-prd-and-ga-criteria.json
- Console workflows spec (create/start/stop/rollback): sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/console-route-ab-testing-workflows.json
- Metrics schema (what we can visualize without inventing fields): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/ab-testing-metrics-schema-v1.json
- Dashboard mockups (early): sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/observability/ab-testing-dashboard-mockups.json
- Applied ML guidance on quality deltas and caveats: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/ab-quality-metrics-stat-plan.json

Design deliverables:
1) Results dashboard IA + component spec:
   - Layout, navigation (tabs/sections), empty states, loading states, and error states.
   - Clear definitions of each metric (tooltip microcopy).
2) Confidence indicator pattern:
   - Proposed pattern + thresholds + copy.
   - Alignment with Applied ML (Sana) on what we can claim in UI.
3) Filtering pattern:
   - Filter location, chip behavior, persistence (URL params), and “Reset to defaults.”
4) Accessibility checklist for chart components and tables.

Acceptance criteria:
- Variant comparison cards are understandable at a glance (control vs variant) and show deltas with consistent formatting.
- Users can filter by region and time range without losing context.
- Confidence indicator includes explicit caveats and links to “How we compute this” (help panel).
- WCAG AA color contrast is met; keyboard navigation works across the entire page; charts have accessible summaries.

Open questions:
- Confidence: do we label as “Low / Medium / High” or show a neutral “Data quality” signal (e.g., “Enough data”) to avoid stats misinterpretation?
- Default metric set for summary row: latency p95 + error rate + cost per request + exposures?
- Should we show guardrail threshold overlays (e.g., latency regression limit) directly on charts, or only in a separate “Guardrails” panel?
- How do we represent ‘paused’ experiments in the time series (gap vs shaded region)?

Stakeholders:

Notes:
- Avoid implying causality; the dashboard is an operational comparison view. Statistical rigor for eval suite comparisons should be clearly labeled as “offline eval results” and separated from online latency/cost/error telemetry.
comments: 2026-02-07 (Kenji Nakamura): Started consolidating the engineering dashboard mockups into Console-native components. Main gap: mockups assume we can query percentiles + TTFT at arbitrary breakdowns; need to confirm what ENG-2844 will materialize by experiment_id + variant_id + region + time_bucket without cardinality blowups.

2026-02-10 (Allison Grant): Please ensure we have a chart-free accessible mode. At minimum, every chart needs a ‘View as table’ affordance and a screen-reader summary (e.g., “Variant B p95 latency is 412ms, +8% vs control”). Also watch contrast on delta badges.

2026-02-12 (Sana Farid): Re: confidence: please do not call it “statistical significance” for online telemetry. Recommend a “Confidence” or “Data sufficiency” indicator keyed off exposure count + stability of estimates (e.g., wide intervals). If we show intervals, label them explicitly and add an explainer. For eval suite deltas, we can use confidence intervals, but must note multiple comparisons and minimum sample size.

2026-02-14 (Marissa Cole): Strong preference for a single ‘Executive summary’ row (latency p95, error rate, cost/request, exposures) before deep charts. Also need region filter because design partners are comparing eu-west vs us-east behavior.

2026-02-18 (Kenji Nakamura): Drafted component spec: (1) Summary header, (2) KPI comparison grid, (3) Trends tab (time series), (4) Breakdowns tab (region small multiples), (5) Quality tab (offline eval results) gated by whether an eval suite is attached. Added empty state copy for no exposures and for telemetry delay (up to ~5–10m).

2026-02-20 (Tessa Morgan): Review feedback: keep deltas consistent (always show ‘vs Control’), use neutral colors for control and accent for variant; do not encode good/bad by color. Add a persistent ‘Definitions’ side panel (drawer) for p95/TTFT, tokens/request, error types, and how exposure is counted.

2026-02-23 (Kenji Nakamura): Addressed a11y feedback: added table views for each chart section, specified keyboard focus order for filter bar + tabs + tooltips, and added text alternative requirements for any icon-only deltas. Marking In Review pending PM + Applied ML sign-off on confidence copy.
